Key findings
Funded with $1B entirely from Amazon's balance sheet; contrasts with OpenAI's ~$4B deployment JV (TPG/Advent/Bain/Brookfield) and Anthropic's ~$1.5B JV (Blackstone/Goldman/Hellman & Friedman), both of which required PE partners. No LP return pressure.

What they do
FDE model · approach · differentiation
Core model
Pods of 5-6 AWS engineers embed inside enterprise customers and build production AI systems in the customer's own AWS environment rather than advising. Engagements run on the 45/45/45 framework and transfer capability: customers retain deployed agentic workflows, a governed versioned knowledge graph, semantic-layer architecture, MCP servers, runbooks, architectural documentation, and trained internal engineering champions. Customer teams progress from observers (week 1) to co-builders (weeks 2-4) to autonomous operators (post-engagement). VP Francessca Vasquez frames the scope as taking a business workflow end-to-end, not isolated use cases.
Methodology: AI-DLC
The AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) governs all engagements. AI agents generate plans, code, tests, and infrastructure configurations; humans verify and approve each execution step, shifting the developer role from writing code to validating AI-generated output. AWS used its own agentic coding tool, Amazon Kiro, to rebuild the Bedrock inference engine in 76 days against an original 40-engineer/1-year estimate.
Durable deliverables
Deployed inside the customer's AWS account and customer-controlled: a versioned knowledge graph with domain ontology; a semantic layer connecting enterprise data sources to that graph; MCP servers for agent tool access; agent-operations tooling, capability registries, and evaluation frameworks; runbooks and architectural documentation; and trained internal engineering champions who maintain and extend the systems.
Pricing
Outcome-based fixed pricing, not billable hours; no public rate card or price floor for direct engagements. The Innovative Solutions (AWS Premier Partner) implementation provides a public reference structure: (1) AI Assessment, a fixed-price readiness evaluation and POC build; (2) POD (Product-Oriented Delivery), fixed-price production workflow delivery with an optional success bonus paid only on defined outcomes; (3) FDS Retainer, a monthly embedded-engineer retainer with performance bonuses tied to cost-efficiency targets.
Partner-led tier
Launched simultaneously through the AWS Partner Network. Premier Partners who pass a production-engineering technical bar field ring-fenced, AWS-credentialed FDE teams under Strategic Collaboration Agreements. Partners receive and permanently own a delivery harness (MCP servers, agent-operations tooling, architecture agents, governance-operations layers, capability registries), multiplying coverage without proportional AWS headcount growth.
Target customers
Fortune 500 enterprises already running significant AWS workloads in regulated, data-intensive verticals: sports and media (NBA, NFL), automotive and logistics (Cox Automotive, BMW, Southwest Airlines), life sciences and research (Allen Institute), manufacturing and imaging (Ricoh, Jabil), and technology services (Lyft). Constellation Research also cites financial services, healthcare, and public sector as target verticals. Not aimed at startups or sub-$100M-revenue companies for direct engagement.
Pricing model
Outcome-based fixed pricing, not billable hours; no public rate card for direct engagements, likely bundled or subsidized within large AWS enterprise agreements. Partner reference tiers (via Innovative Solutions): fixed-price AI Assessment; fixed-price POD delivery with optional success bonus; monthly FDS Retainer with cost-efficiency performance bonuses.
Tech stack
Amazon Bedrock and Bedrock AgentCore (GA Apr 22, 2026; 1M+ SDK downloads at GA) as the agent deployment and operations platform; MCP servers for agent tool access; Amazon Kiro agentic coding tool; versioned knowledge graphs, semantic layers, capability registries, and evaluation frameworks, all deployed inside the customer's own AWS account under the AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC).
